Method
Cook step by step

One step at a time, with ingredients and timers close at hand.

01
Prepare the apples

Wash and peel the apples, then grate them on the coarse side of a grater. Do not grate them finely, or they will release too much juice.

CHECKPOINTThe apples are in distinct coarse shreds rather than a fine, wet pulp.

02
Mix the batter

Crack the eggs directly into the grated apples. Add the kefir or yoghurt and the sugar, or the mashed banana instead of sugar, then mix. Add the Schär Mix B Bread flour and bicarbonate of soda and stir until combined.

2–3 MIN PER SIDE · MEDIUM HEAT

03
Fry the fritters

TIPLower the heat if the outside browns before the top begins to set.

Heat a little oil in a frying pan. Spoon 1 tablespoon of batter per fritter into the hot pan and fry over medium heat for 2–3 minutes per side, so the apples have time to cook through.

CHECKPOINTTurn when the underside is golden and the top has begun to set around the edges; the centre should no longer look wet after the second side cooks.

CELEBRATION CAKE

Gluten-Free
Napoleon Cake

Two cakes with six thin 28 cm layers each, warm custard and nuts.

Tested

Made many times.

ACTIVE TIME
1 hour
YIELD
2 cakes
DIFFICULTY
Advanced

Best served the next day.

FLOUR
Schär Mix B + tapioca and corn starch
Jump to ingredients
Jump to steps

BEFORE YOU START

Plan for the rest.
Keep this in mind

Have enough sheets of baking parchment for 12 layers: each is rolled between two sheets and baked on the lower one.

Keep this in mind

Plan a day ahead: the dough discs chill for at least 2 hours, and the assembled cake rests for 1 hour at room temperature and 12–24 hours in the refrigerator.

METHOD · 19 STEPS

Make it step by step.
Cook step by step

One step at a time, with ingredients and timers close at hand.

5–10 SEC

01
Mix the dry ingredients

In a food processor, mix the Schär Mix B, both starches, xanthan, baking powder, salt and sugar for 5–10 seconds.

10–15 MIN

02
Cut in the cold butter

Cube the cold butter, freeze it for 10–15 minutes, add it to the dry mixture and pulse about ten times.

CHECKPOINTThe crumb should be uneven: some sandy, with some pea-sized pieces of butter.

1
2
3
03
Mix the wet ingredients

Mix the eggs, chosen cultured dairy, sunflower oil and lemon juice only until smooth.

04
Bring the dough together

Pour the liquid into the dry mixture and combine with short pulses. Add cold water as needed.

CHECKPOINTThe dough should gather into clumps, feel pliable and not become a sticky paste.

1
2
05
Fold the dough

Quickly bring the dough together by hand, fold it 2–3 times and shape it into a disc. Do not knead for long.

AT LEAST 2 HOURS

06
Divide and chill

Divide the dough into twelve discs, wrap each one and chill for at least 2 hours; they may be left overnight.

5–10 MIN

07
Soften one disc

Take out one disc at a time. If it is very firm, leave it on the counter for 5–10 minutes.

08
Roll and trim a layer

TIPRoll the layer on the parchment used for baking so the thin dough does not need to be transferred.

Roll the disc between two sheets of parchment to about 1.5 mm thick. Cut a 28 cm circle, leave the scraps beside it and prick with a fork.

7–10 MIN · 190°C

09
Bake the layer

Bake the layer with its scraps at 190°C for about 7–10 minutes.

CHECKPOINTThe layer should be light golden.

10
Heat the milk

Set aside 600–650 ml of cold milk. Heat the remaining milk until almost boiling.

11
Mix the custard base

In a large bowl, combine the sugar, both starches, vanilla sugar and salt. Add the reserved cold milk and stir until smooth, then add the four eggs.

12
Temper the egg mixture

Whisk 2–3 ladlefuls of hot milk into the egg and starch mixture, then return everything to the saucepan.

30–60 SEC

13
Cook the custard

Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly. After the first bubbles appear, cook for another 30–60 seconds.

CHECKPOINTStart the final 30–60 seconds when the first bubbles appear.

14
Add the butter

Remove the custard from the heat, add the butter and stir until smooth.

8–10 MIN · 160°C

15
Toast the walnuts

Toast the walnuts at 160°C for 8–10 minutes.

4–5 MIN · 160°C

16
Toast the almonds

Toast the flaked almonds at 160°C for 4–5 minutes.

17
Assemble the cakes

Assemble two cakes with six layers each. Use the custard while warm. Spread it on every layer, adding walnuts to every other layer. Finish with layer crumbs and flaked almonds.

1 HOUR

18
Rest at room temperature

After assembly, leave the cake at room temperature for about 1 hour.

12–24 HOURS

19
Chill overnight

Refrigerate the cake for 12–24 hours. It tastes best the next day.
